lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write one comment that builds on: "The character seems patient."

FEEDBACK
Build-on: "Yes — waiting for the light instead of leaving shows patience, especially when..."

CHECK
Talking over others or ignoring the book breaks the circle purpose.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Run a four-turn discussion circle on a shared page. Each turn must include either a new idea or a build-on with evidence. Record one strong evidence link.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Run a four-turn discussion circle on a shared page. Each turn must include either a new idea or a build-on with evidence. Record one strong evidence link. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original demonstration: Speaker A: "The fog made me nervous." Speaker B: "I agree, especially when it says hands shook." Turns stay respectful and linked.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Talking over others or ignoring the book breaks the circle purpose. Correction: Build-on: "Yes — waiting for the light instead of leaving shows patience, especially when..."

Parent: Likely misconception: Talking over others or ignoring the book breaks the circle purpose. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

teach_steps.explain:
A book discussion circle gives each speaker a turn to share ideas and build on others using text evidence.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
